title: Dev/Prod Parity: Mocks Locally, Redirects in Production — Check

questions.prompt: What serves the `/agronomy-api/*` surface during local development?
questions.explanation: Locally, `tools/mock-apis.mjs` serves the gateway and AI surfaces; production uses Netlify redirects to the deployed functions.
options: A live connection to CIMIS and the other real APIs

questions.prompt: A Netlify redirect with `status = 200` rewrites the request so the browser's visible URL still reads `/agronomy-api/...`.
questions.explanation: A 200 rewrite serves the function transparently; the client URL is unchanged, hiding the real function path.

questions.prompt: What most directly preserves dev/prod parity in this setup?
questions.explanation: Parity comes from holding the client-facing contract constant and validating both backends against it, even though the machinery differs.
options: Using the exact same code for the mock and the functions
Keeping the client-visible contract (`/agronomy-api/*` shapes and schemas) identical across environments
